answer: Register on the website (free), review the demo and instructions, and submit the required deposit with the Clerk.
quote: Registration on the website is free. However, you will need to abide by the Clerk's deposit rules. … Register on the website Review the recorded Demo on the Home page Read the Tax Deed Instructions documents Submit the required deposit with the Clerk

answer: Deposit 5% of the anticipated final bid or $200: by ACH at least 3 full business days before the auction, or by money order or cashier's check to the Tax Deed Department by 4:00 p.m. the day before. No deposits on auction day.
quote: If you submit your deposit via ACH/Electronic Debit, it must be submitted at least three (3) full business days before the auction in which you intend to participate. … an ACH/Electronic Debit payment equal to five percent (5%) of the anticipated final bid or $200 … This type of deposit must be presented to the Tax Deed Department by 4:00 p.m. the day before the scheduled auction. … No deposits will be accepted on the day of the auction.
source_title: Online Auctions FAQs - St. Lucie County Clerk of the Circuit Court and Comptroller

answer: The balance must be received by the Clerk by 2:00 pm on the next business day, by cashier's check or wire transfer.
quote: The difference between the successful bidder's deposit and the total amount due must be received by the Clerk by 2:00 pm on the next business day after the sale. … Final payment may be made by cashier's check or wire transfer.

answer: Bidders must register at www.volusia.realtaxdeed.com to get a username and password, and make a deposit for each property they want to bid on.

answer: A non-refundable deposit of 5% of the final bid or $200.00, whichever is greater, is required for each property. ACH deposits are due 4 full working days before the sale; wire transfers by 2:00 PM ET on the business day before the sale.
quote: Bidders must remit their ACH deposit no later than 4 full working days prior to the commencement of a sale or by 2:00 PM ET on the business day before the sale when using wire transfer. … For each piece of property purchased, the successful high bidder is required to pay a non-refundable deposit equal to 5 percent of the final bid or $200.00, whichever is greater, at the time of the sale.
source_title: Tax Deeds - Clerk of the Circuit Court, Volusia County Florida

answer: The balance of the high bid, with the recording fee, documentary stamps and a deposit registry fee, must be received within 24 hours of the sale; a wire transfer no later than 12:00 PM ET on the next business day. Cash is not accepted.
quote: payment of the balance of the high bid, along with the recording fee, state documentary stamps of $.70 per $100.00 of the transfer amount, and a deposit registry fee must be received by the Clerk's office within 24 hours of the sale. … Wire transfer must be received no later than 12:00 PM ET on the next business day after the sale. … the Clerk's Office will no longer accept cash as a means of bidder account deposit, bids or final winning bid payment.
source_title: Tax Deeds - Clerk of the Circuit Court, Volusia County Florida
